name: Standard due dates and the three review cycles
what: Each [activity code](#term:activity-code) has three due dates a year; applications are due by 5:00 PM local time of the [applicant organization](#term:applicant-organization), and dedicated AIDS due dates no longer exist [2](#cite:2) [17](#cite:17).

name: Modular budget
what: A simplified budget format for requests up to $250,000 in direct costs a year, built in $25,000 modules; consortium [F&A](#term:indirect-costs) is left out when testing the threshold, and foreign organizations use a detailed budget instead [36](#cite:36).

name: Salary limitation (salary cap)
what: [NIH](#term:nih) [grant](#term:grant) funds may not pay an individual's salary above [Executive Level II](#term:salary-cap) of the federal pay scale: $225,700 from October 1 to December 31, 2025 and $228,000 from January 1, 2026 [20](#cite:20) [19](#cite:19) [21](#cite:21).

name: Requests of $500,000 or more in direct costs
what: Since December 3, 2025 an [unsolicited](#term:unsolicited-request) application asking $500,000 or more in [direct costs](#term:direct-costs) in any year needs no prior agreement from the institute and no cover letter naming a programme official [37](#cite:37) [36](#cite:36).

name: Facilities and administrative (F&A, indirect) costs
what: [F&A costs](#term:indirect-costs) are paid on top of [direct costs](#term:direct-costs) at the organization's federally [negotiated rate](#term:nicra), fixed for the [competitive segment](#term:budget-period); foreign organizations receive 8 percent, conference [grants](#term:grant) none, and an organization with no negotiated rate may elect a [de minimis rate](#term:de-minimis-rate), given as 10% in the fetched policy text [64](#cite:64) [36](#cite:36).

name: Simplified peer review framework
what: For due dates from January 25, 2025, reviewers of most research project applications score Importance of the Research and Rigor and Feasibility from 1 to 9 and rate Expertise and Resources as sufficient or insufficient [39](#cite:39) [41](#cite:41).

name: Study section (scientific review group)
what: The first level of review; [study sections](#term:study-section) are organized by the [Center for Scientific Review](#term:center-for-scientific-review) and grouped into review branches by discipline [38](#cite:38) [40](#cite:40).

name: 'Competitive but not discussed' designation
what: Under the modified review practices in force through the January 2027 council round, about 30-35 percent of applications are discussed and the committee's middle third is labelled 'competitive but not discussed' [16](#cite:16) [84](#cite:84) [85](#cite:85).

name: Advisory council review (second level)
what: The [national advisory council](#term:advisory-council) or board of the institute gives the second level of review and makes recommendations to the director, who decides [38](#cite:38) [15](#cite:15).

name: Unified funding strategy (no paylines)
what: From the January 2026 council round, institutes do not rely on [paylines](#term:payline); funding policies follow six tenets and each institute publishes the factors it weighs [123](#cite:123) [15](#cite:15).

name: Just-in-time information
what: Extra information [NIH](#term:nih) may request when an application is under consideration for funding; a request is not an indicator of an award decision [122](#cite:122).

name: Notice of Award (NoA)
what: The official award document; the recipient accepts by drawing down or requesting funds and is then bound by the [NIH Grants Policy Statement](#term:nih-grants-policy-statement) unless the notice says otherwise [122](#cite:122) [118](#cite:118).

name: Highlighted Topics
what: Research areas an institute, center or office wants to see; they are not funding opportunities and carry no guaranteed funds, and nobody applies 'to' a topic: the application goes in through a [parent announcement](#term:parent-announcement) or another broad notice [11](#cite:11) [142](#cite:142) [94](#cite:94).

name: Six applications per investigator per calendar year
what: [NIH](#term:nih) accepts six new, [renewal](#term:renewal), [resubmission](#term:resubmission) or revision applications from one [PD/PI](#term:principal-investigator) or [multiple PD/PI](#term:multiple-pi) per calendar year, for all [activity codes](#term:activity-code) except T codes and R13, for applications submitted on or after September 25, 2025 [12](#cite:12).

name: AI use in applications
what: [NIH](#term:nih) does not treat an application substantially developed by AI, or with sections substantially developed by AI, as the applicant's original ideas; AI found after award may lead to referral to the Office of Research Integrity and enforcement actions [12](#cite:12) [140](#cite:140).

name: Multi-year (up-front) funding of awards
what: A multi-year funded award is paid in full at the start of the [project period](#term:budget-period) from one fiscal year's [appropriation](#term:appropriations-act); section 240 of the FY 2026 appropriations act limits FY 2026 obligations for such awards to no more than the FY 2025 amount [137](#cite:137) [21](#cite:21).

name: Late applications
what: A late application may be considered case by case if submitted within two calendar weeks of the due date; continuous submission ended May 25, 2026 [130](#cite:130).

name: PHS Assignment Request Form
what: The optional form an applicant uses to ask for assignment to a particular institute and review group [94](#cite:94) [97](#cite:97).

name: Cooperative agreement (U codes)
what: [Financial assistance](#term:financial-assistance) in which [NIH](#term:nih) staff are substantially involved after award; the terms of each notice name the NIH roles and a dispute panel [106](#cite:106) [116](#cite:116).

name: Foreign component (and the end of foreign subawards)
what: A foreign component is any significant scientific element of a project performed outside the United States; [NIH](#term:nih) no longer makes awards that include a [subaward](#term:subaward) to a foreign entity, and paid foreign collaborators are funded through linked awards [106](#cite:106) [22](#cite:22) [86](#cite:86).

name: Termination terms
what: Award terms effective October 1, 2025 and the March 2026 [Grants](#term:grant) Policy Statement say [NIH](#term:nih) may terminate an award, to the extent authorized by law, if it determines the award no longer effectuates programme goals or agency priorities [65](#cite:65) [139](#cite:139).

name: Programme description, programme announcement, solicitation, Dear Colleague Letter
what: A programme description is a broad, general description of a programme that uses the [PAPPG](#term:pappg)'s generic eligibility and preparation rules [156](#cite:156). A programme announcement is a formal [NSF](#term:nsf) publication announcing a programme, also on the generic rules [156](#cite:156). A [programme solicitation](#term:program-solicitation) is more focused, applies for a limited period, and is used when NSF departs from the generic rules — limiting who may submit or how many proposals, restricting [indirect costs](#term:indirect-costs), requiring [preliminary proposals](#term:pre-application), adding review criteria or requiring [cost sharing](#term:cost-sharing) [156](#cite:156) [158](#cite:158). A [Dear Colleague Letter](#term:dear-colleague-letter) gives information, clarifies policy, or announces interest in planning, RAPID, [EAGER](#term:eager-rapid), RAISE or conference proposals or [supplements](#term:supplement) on a topic [156](#cite:156) [158](#cite:158). In August 2026 NSF called its twelve new solicitations [Notices of Funding Opportunity](#term:nofo) [192](#cite:192).

name: Concept outline
what: A concise summary of a project idea sent before certain proposal types so that a [programme officer](#term:program-officer) can judge fit; it goes by email or through the ProSPCT tool and is generally limited to two pages or 6000 characters [156](#cite:156) [250](#cite:250).

name: Letter of intent
what: A non-binding notice some [solicitations](#term:program-solicitation) require so that staff can gauge the size of a competition; if a required letter is missing the full proposal is not accepted [156](#cite:156).

name: Preliminary proposal
what: A short first-stage proposal some [solicitations](#term:program-solicitation) require; the outcome is either a binding invite or not-invite decision, or an advisory encourage or discourage [156](#cite:156). Expeditions in Computing uses one [191](#cite:191).

name: Target date, deadline date, submission window, accepted anytime
what: After a target date a proposal is still accepted but may miss a panel; after a deadline date it is not accepted; the end of a submission window is treated as a deadline [156](#cite:156). Deadlines are 5 p.m. submitting organisation's local time [156](#cite:156).

name: Merit review
what: Review against [Intellectual Merit and Broader Impacts](#term:intellectual-merit), with five elements considered under each; reviewers are ad hoc, panel or both, and since December 8, 2025 at least two reviewers, who may be [NSF](#term:nsf) staff, are required [157](#cite:157) [149](#cite:149). The National Science Board recommended in 2025 pursuing a rename of Broader Impacts to Societal Benefits [271](#cite:271).

name: Return without review
what: [NSF](#term:nsf) returns a proposal unreviewed for listed reasons, among them missing sections, a missed deadline, duplication, and not being responsive to the funding opportunity; Supplement 1 added lacking sufficient content to permit effective [merit review](#term:merit-review) [258](#cite:258) [149](#cite:149). NSF also uses the mechanism for proposals it judges not aligned with agency priorities [154](#cite:154).

name: Reconsideration of a declined proposal
what: A [PI](#term:principal-investigator) may ask the Assistant Director for reconsideration within 90 days of a declination, and the Deputy Director within 60 days after that answer; fellowship, RAPID and [EAGER](#term:eager-rapid) declinations are excluded [258](#cite:258).

name: Senior personnel salary: the two-month limit
what: Salary requested for each senior/key person is limited to two months of regular salary in any one year [257](#cite:257).

name: Indirect (F&A) costs
what: [Indirect costs](#term:indirect-costs) are budgeted at the organisation's federally [negotiated rate](#term:nicra) unless a [solicitation](#term:program-solicitation) says otherwise [257](#cite:257). The [15 percent cap](#term:indirect-rate-cap) [NSF](#term:nsf) announced in May 2025 was [vacated](#term:vacatur) by a court and is not in effect [237](#cite:237) [238](#cite:238). The [Grant](#term:grant) General Conditions of July 31, 2026 hold an [institution of higher education](#term:institution-of-higher-education) to the negotiated rate in effect at the time of the initial award [263](#cite:263). The [PAPPG](#term:pappg) states that recipients are entitled to reimbursement of indirect costs allocable to the NSF share of allowable [direct costs](#term:direct-costs) [260](#cite:260).

name: Cost sharing
what: Voluntary committed [cost sharing](#term:cost-sharing) is prohibited [257](#cite:257). [NSF](#term:nsf)'s cost-sharing page says only a small number of programmes require cost sharing [164](#cite:164) [162](#cite:162).

variants.what: From April 27, 2026 the plan is created with a tool in [Research.gov](#term:research-gov), without the former two-page limit; recipients share all data supporting NSF-funded publications at the time of publication, and exceptions are justified in the plan [150](#cite:150).

name: NSF Data Management and Sharing Plan (DMSP)
what: [NSF](#term:nsf) proposals carry a [Data Management and Sharing Plan](#term:data-management-plan) that describes how the project will meet NSF's policy on dissemination and sharing of research results [150](#cite:150). Guidance on its content varies by [directorate](#term:nsf-directorate) [2032](#cite:2032).
rule: Under Supplement 2 to [PAPPG](#term:pappg) 24-1, issued and effective January 22, 2026, the plan is created with a tool in Research.gov from April 27, 2026, replacing a document of no more than two pages; proposals submitted before that date upload a PDF [150](#cite:150). Recipients share all data supporting NSF-funded publications at the time of publication, and any exception is described and justified in the plan [150](#cite:150). A change to the plan that changes the objectives or scope needs the [programme officer](#term:program-officer)'s [prior written approval](#term:prior-approval) [150](#cite:150).

applies_to: NSF proposals and awards [150](#cite:150).

name: No-cost extension
what: A recipient may extend a [grant](#term:grant) once by up to 12 months on notice to [NSF](#term:nsf) at least ten calendar days before the end date; a further extension needs NSF approval requested at least 45 days before the end date [259](#cite:259).

name: Termination terms
what: [NSF](#term:nsf) may terminate an award for failure to comply with its terms or because it no longer effectuates the programme goals or agency priorities [261](#cite:261) [263](#cite:263). The [PAPPG](#term:pappg) gives 30 days to ask for review, and the 2026 General Conditions include a [termination](#term:termination) review procedure [261](#cite:261) [263](#cite:263). NSF's priorities page states that appeals of the 2025 terminations will not be reviewed or considered [154](#cite:154).

name: Other proposal types listed in PAPPG Chapter II.F
what: Besides planning, RAPID, [EAGER](#term:eager-rapid), RAISE, GOALI and conference proposals, Chapter II.F lists Ideas Lab, FASED, equipment, travel, centre and research infrastructure proposals, and supplemental requests for Career-Life Balance and for Research Opportunity Awards [257](#cite:257). Supplement 1 added the SBIR/STTR Project Pitch as a type of submission [149](#cite:149).

name: Broad agency announcement (BAA)
what: A standing defence notice that invites research proposals across an office's interests and can lead to a [grant](#term:grant), [cooperative agreement](#term:cooperative-agreement), contract or other transaction [334](#cite:334) [323](#cite:323).

name: White paper (DoD)
what: A short description sent before a proposal so that a [programme officer](#term:program-officer) can encourage or discourage it. ONR limits it to 5 pages [334](#cite:334); ARL strongly encourages but does not require it [341](#cite:341); MURI calls it optional but strongly recommended [325](#cite:325).

name: Pre-application (DOE Office of Science)
what: A preliminary research description sent through [PAMS](#term:doe-pams); required for certain review panels and optional otherwise in the FY 2027 annual notice [277](#cite:277) [278](#cite:278).

name: Concept paper and reply to reviewer comments (ARPA-E)
what: ARPA-E's first stage is a [concept paper](#term:concept-outline); after the full application ARPA-E releases reviewer comments and the applicant may reply by a set date [301](#cite:301). A 'discourage' notice on a concept paper does not bar a full application [302](#cite:302).

name: Pre-application and letter of intent (CDMRP)
what: Every [CDMRP](#term:cdmrp) application starts with a [pre-application](#term:pre-application) in [eBRAP](#term:ebrap); in the two FY26 announcements read it is a [letter of intent](#term:letter-of-intent) [330](#cite:330) [356](#cite:356).

name: Two-tier review (CDMRP)
what: [Peer review](#term:merit-review) for merit and impact, then programmatic review that compares meritorious applications against the programme's goals; consumer reviewers vote [352](#cite:352).

name: Application verification period (CDMRP)
what: A short period after the deadline when the applicant checks the application in [eBRAP](#term:ebrap); for the FY26 BCRP Breakthrough Award it ends November 25, 2026 [356](#cite:356).

name: Dual-anonymous peer review (NASA)
what: Reviewers are not told who the proposers are until rating is complete; the proposer writes an anonymized proposal and a separate document on expertise and resources [375](#cite:375).

name: Notice of intent and Step-1 proposal (NASA)
what: Many [ROSES](#term:roses) elements require a notice of intent or a Step-1 proposal before the full proposal; a proposal without a required on-time notice is returned without review [377](#cite:377) [374](#cite:374).

name: No exchange of funds (NASA)
what: Research by a non-U.S. organisation within a U.S. proposal is normally supported without NASA money passing to the foreign organisation [380](#cite:380).

variants.what: An entity that has never had a [negotiated indirect cost rate](#term:nicra) may charge 15% of [modified total direct costs](#term:mtdc) under the ONR and MURI announcements [334](#cite:334) [325](#cite:325).

The rate an organization without a negotiated indirect cost rate may charge. The [HHS](#term:hhs) [Grants](#term:grant) Policy Statement sets it at 15% of modified total direct costs; [HRSA](#term:hrsa) records that HHS raised it from 10 to 15 percent effective October 1, 2024. The [OJP](#term:office-of-justice-programs) guide as fetched gives 10 percent [528](#cite:528) [529](#cite:529) [619](#cite:619).

A recipient that does not have a current negotiated indirect cost rate may elect to charge a [de minimis rate](#term:de-minimis-rate) of up to 15 percent of modified total direct costs ([2 CFR 200](#term:uniform-guidance).414(f)) [2070](#cite:2070). [NSF](#term:nsf)'s page says the 15% rate may be elected for any award executed on or after October 1, 2024, and that it is applied consistently across all of the organisation's federal awards until the organisation negotiates a rate [163](#cite:163). The [eCFR](#term:cfr) text of 200.414 current to 10/01/2026 carries the same rate, and USDA's General Terms and Conditions effective December 31, 2025 state it as 15 percent of modified total direct costs [1802](#cite:1802) [1948](#cite:1948).

name: De minimis indirect cost rate
what: The de minimis rate lets an organisation with no current federally negotiated rate charge [indirect costs](#term:indirect-costs) at a flat percentage without negotiating [1802](#cite:1802). The rate in force is up to 15 percent of modified total direct costs [1802](#cite:1802). This 15 percent is an option for organisations that have no negotiated rate; it is a different thing from the 15 percent caps that four agencies tried to place on negotiated rates in 2025 [1802](#cite:1802) [24](#cite:24).
rule: Under 2 CFR 200.414(f) a recipient or [subrecipient](#term:subrecipient) that does not have a current federal negotiated indirect cost rate may elect a de minimis rate of up to 15 percent of modified total direct costs; no documentation is needed to justify it, and it may be used indefinitely [1802](#cite:1802). A [pass-through entity](#term:pass-through-entity) may not require a subrecipient that has a federally negotiated rate to use the de minimis rate instead [1823](#cite:1823). The award document states the indirect cost rate, including whether the de minimis rate is charged [1810](#cite:1810). NSF states that recipients may elect the 15% rate for any award executed on or after October 1, 2024 and that the rate must be applied consistently across all of an organisation's federal awards [163](#cite:163). HHS states the de minimis rate as 15% of modified total direct costs [528](#cite:528). A second reading of 200.414 on the eCFR on 2026-10-04, in the text current to 10/01/2026, returned the same rate of up to 15 percent of modified total direct costs in paragraph (f) [1802](#cite:1802). [OMB](#term:omb)'s [proposed rule](#term:proposed-rule) would have each award show the indirect cost rate, including whether the de minimis rate is charged under 200.414 [2104](#cite:2104).

A programme whose statute or notice sets a lower limit, such as the 8 percent HHS limit on [training grants](#term:t32), is governed by that limit [1884](#cite:1884).

name: Energy Policy Act cost share (DOE)
what: At least 20 percent for research and development and 50 percent for demonstration or commercial application, with an exclusion for basic or fundamental research [299](#cite:299).

name: DoD Grant and Agreement Regulations (DoDGARs)
what: The rules for DoD [grants](#term:grant) and [cooperative agreements](#term:cooperative-agreement). 2 [CFR](#term:cfr) part 1104 carries the governmentwide [Uniform Guidance](#term:uniform-guidance) into DoD awards on an interim basis [332](#cite:332); 32 CFR part 22 requires merit-based competitive procedures and impartial review against the criteria in the notice [333](#cite:333). Award terms are in the DoD Research and Development General Terms and Conditions with each office's addendum [338](#cite:338).

name: DOE research, technology and economic security review
what: DOE reviews technical descriptions, biographical sketches, [current and pending support](#term:other-support) and foreign-connection disclosures for risk, and may require certifications, mitigation agreements, reporting or special terms [368](#cite:368). The [Office of Science](#term:doe-office-of-science) notice bars Entities of Concern from projects [278](#cite:278).

name: NASA grant rules: 2 CFR 1800, the GCAM and the terms and conditions
what: NASA adopts the [Uniform Guidance](#term:uniform-guidance) in 2 [CFR](#term:cfr) part 1800 [385](#cite:385); the [Grant](#term:grant) and [Cooperative Agreement](#term:cooperative-agreement) Manual of March 2025 is the governing guide and the January 2026 terms and conditions apply to awards [379](#cite:379) [380](#cite:380) [381](#cite:381).

name: Letter of intent
what: A short notice sent before the application. [AFRI](#term:nifa) workshop [grants](#term:grant) require one; AFRI Strengthening Agricultural Systems, the 2025 University Transportation Centers recompetition and the 2026 NCCOS notice each set a [letter of intent](#term:letter-of-intent) deadline; the FY 2026 RISA notice made it optional [412](#cite:412) [404](#cite:404) [493](#cite:493) [477](#cite:477) [434](#cite:434).

name: Pre-application
what: A first-stage application that decides who is invited to submit in full. The Specialty Crop Research Initiative judges [pre-applications](#term:pre-application) by industry relevance; NIST's Precision Measurement [Grant](#term:grant) Program reviews pre-applications before full applications [414](#cite:414) [471](#cite:471).

name: NIFA statutory indirect cost limit
what: [NIFA](#term:nifa) competitive awards carry a statutory limit on [indirect costs](#term:indirect-costs). The FY 2026 AFRI and Specialty Crop notices state it as 30 percent of Total Federal Funds Awarded under section 1462 of NARETPA (7 U.S.C. 3310), applied as the lesser of the [negotiated rate](#term:nicra) or that limit and counting sub-awardee indirect costs [412](#cite:412) [414](#cite:414) [407](#cite:407).

name: NIFA matching requirements
what: Several [NIFA](#term:nifa) programmes require a non-federal match: at least equal to the award for the Specialty Crop Research Initiative (waivable in two cases), 100% as listed for Organic Agriculture Research and Extension, and for AFRI only for equipment [grants](#term:grant) and commodity-specific applied research not of national scope [414](#cite:414) [415](#cite:415) [417](#cite:417).

name: AFRI mentoring plan
what: New in FY 2026: a mentoring plan is required for [AFRI](#term:nifa) applications that involve education, training or mentoring of students or others; workshop, equipment and sabbatical [grants](#term:grant) are excluded [404](#cite:404).

pending_changes.text: [OMB](#term:omb)'s [proposed rule](#term:proposed-rule) lists a revised 200.205 on agency review of the merit of proposals; an association summary says it would write senior appointee review of each notice into the regulation and describe [peer review](#term:merit-review) as advisory [1458](#cite:1458) [1878](#cite:1878).

The chair of the Senate [Appropriations](#term:appropriations-act) Committee wrote to the OMB and [NIH](#term:nih) Directors on September 22, 2026 about an [executive order](#term:executive-order) reported to be in preparation that would add a review of NIH [grant](#term:grant) applications after merit review; no such order was found in this sweep [1892](#cite:1892).

Read in the [Federal Register](#term:federal-register) text of OMB's proposal: proposed 200.205 would establish a pre-issuance review, described as consistent with [Executive Order 14332](#term:executive-order-14332), in which senior appointees review proposals selected for funding against applicable law, agency priorities and the national interest; the review must be described in the [notice of funding opportunity](#term:nofo) and may form the basis of a decision not to select an applicant; peer review remains advisory [2092](#cite:2092) [2093](#cite:2093) [2104](#cite:2104).

variants.what: Executive Order 14332 requires each agency head to designate a senior appointee to run a review of new funding opportunity announcements and [discretionary grants](#term:discretionary-grant) for consistency with agency priorities and the national interest. How each agency in this slice carries this out was not found on the pages read [246](#cite:246).

name: Senior appointee review of funding announcements and awards
what: Since Executive Order 14332 a senior appointee in each agency reviews new funding opportunity announcements and discretionary grants before they issue [246](#cite:246). The review sits on top of merit or peer review and checks consistency with agency priorities and the national interest [246](#cite:246).
rule: Section 3 of the order requires each agency head to designate a senior appointee to run the review; the order defines a senior appointee as an individual appointed by the President, a non-career member of the Senior Executive Service, or an employee in a Senior Level, Scientific and Professional, or Grade 15 position in Schedule C of the excepted service [246](#cite:246). The process must include the appointee's approval of announcements, review by subject-matter experts for scientific research, review before awards issue, and coordination between agencies to remove duplication [246](#cite:246). The appointee also reviews discretionary awards each year for consistency with agency priorities and substantial progress [246](#cite:246). Section 4 says appointees are not to ministerially ratify or routinely defer to what others propose [246](#cite:246). DOE's implementing procedures of February 19, 2026 cover funding announcements only [314](#cite:314).
applies_to: Discretionary funding announcements and awards at every executive agency [246](#cite:246).

name: HHS Grants Policy Statement
what: The governing policy for awards from [HHS](#term:hhs) agencies other than [NIH](#term:nih). Version 2.0 took effect October 1, 2025 and applies to awards and funded modifications made on or after that date; on the same date HHS adopted [2 CFR 200](#term:uniform-guidance) with modifications at 2 [CFR](#term:cfr) 300 [527](#cite:527) [528](#cite:528).

name: AHRQ special emphasis notice
what: A notice in which [AHRQ](#term:ahrq) announces interest in a research topic to be pursued through its standing announcements, such as NOT-HS-25-012 on emergency department boarding. With the standing announcements expired in March 2026, no open mechanism was found for responding to one [519](#cite:519) [509](#cite:509) [518](#cite:518).

name: Notice of early expiration
what: A notice that ends a funding announcement before its stated expiration date. [AHRQ](#term:ahrq)'s March 2026 notices took effect immediately and stated that no further applications would be accepted [515](#cite:515) [512](#cite:512).

variants.what: A DOJ applicant submits the [SF-424](#term:sf-424) in [Grants.gov](#term:grants-gov) by one deadline and the rest of the application in [JustGrants](#term:justgrants) by a later one; [OJP](#term:office-of-justice-programs) advises submitting each at least 48 hours early [619](#cite:619) [613](#cite:613).

name: DOJ two-step application (Grants.gov, then JustGrants)
what: A Department of Justice application is submitted in two steps with two deadlines: the SF-424 (and the [SF-LLL](#term:lobbying-certification) where lobbying is disclosed) in Grants.gov, then the full application in JustGrants [619](#cite:619).
rule: Step one must be complete before step two can begin, because the JustGrants account invitation is sent to the address in section 8F of the SF-424, within 24 hours [619](#cite:619). A late application is considered only for a documented technical failure of a government system, reported within 24 hours of the deadline concerned [619](#cite:619).

name: NIJ research independence and integrity statement and data plan
what: NIJ research applications include a statement on research and evaluation independence and integrity, covering conflicts of interest, and a Data Management, Sharing, and Archiving Plan of no more than two pages [605](#cite:605) [619](#cite:619).

name: Invited to apply notice (DOJ)
what: A DOJ notice open only to recipients the agency has invited, such as those named in the congressional joint explanatory statement or a single named organization. It is not an open competition [611](#cite:611) [617](#cite:617).

name: PCORI letter of intent
what: [PCORI](#term:pcori) requires a [letter of intent](#term:letter-of-intent) by a fixed deadline; applicants are notified of its status and only then may submit a full application [599](#cite:599) [591](#cite:591).

name: Objective review with point scores (FDA, HRSA, ACL, ACF)
what: [HHS](#term:hhs) agencies other than [NIH](#term:nih) and [AHRQ](#term:ahrq) score research applications against criteria with points fixed in each notice, by a panel the agency convenes, in place of NIH-style [study sections](#term:study-section) [564](#cite:564) [574](#cite:574) [578](#cite:578) [628](#cite:628).

name: NEH outright funds and federal matching funds
what: Most [NEH](#term:neh) programmes award outright funds only [644](#cite:644) [634](#cite:634). Where a notice offers federal [matching funds](#term:cost-sharing), the applicant budgets the outright request, the federal match and any required cost share separately; cost sharing is required only when matching funds are requested [644](#cite:644) [634](#cite:634).

name: NEH review chain: panel, staff, National Council, Chair
what: Seven steps from preparation to notification; panelists rate Excellent, Very Good, Good, Some Merit or Not Competitive; the Council must by law review applications; the Chair decides [638](#cite:638).

name: De minimis indirect cost rate of 15 percent
what: [NEH](#term:neh), [IMLS](#term:imls) and [IES](#term:ies) each let an applicant without a [negotiated rate](#term:nicra) charge a [de minimis indirect cost rate](#term:de-minimis-rate) of 15 percent of [modified total direct costs](#term:mtdc) [644](#cite:644) [677](#cite:677) [663](#cite:663). NHPRC does not allow [grant](#term:grant) funds to be used for [indirect costs](#term:indirect-costs) at all [698](#cite:698).

name: NEA two-part application
what: Part 1 is submitted through [Grants.gov](#term:grants-gov) and Part 2 through the [NEA](#term:nea) Applicant Portal; in the FY27 cycle the two deadlines were March 23 and April 2, 2026 [651](#cite:651) [650](#cite:650).

name: NEA 1:1 nonfederal cost share
what: An [NEA](#term:nea) award cannot exceed 50% of total project cost; every award requires a nonfederal [cost share](#term:cost-sharing) of at least 1 to 1 [651](#cite:651) [652](#cite:652).

name: IMLS cost share by project type
what: [IMLS](#term:imls) sets [cost share](#term:cost-sharing) by project type: research projects in both National Leadership [Grants](#term:grant) programmes need none; non-research museum projects need 1:1; library National Implementation requests above $299,999 need 1:1 [677](#cite:677) [681](#cite:681).

name: IES letter of intent
what: [IES](#term:ies) sets a [letter of intent](#term:letter-of-intent) date ahead of the deadline, with submission at iesreview.ed.gov; for the FY 2027 first tranche the letter was due September 3, 2026 and the application October 1, 2026 [663](#cite:663) [715](#cite:715).

name: IES peer review scoring and triage
what: Each application has at least two reviewers; criteria are scored 1 (poor) to 7 (excellent); the overall score runs from 1.0 (outstanding) to 5.0 (poor) and is not an average; only the most competitive applications are discussed by the full panel [667](#cite:667).

name: IES public access and data sharing
what: [IES](#term:ies) grantees upload accepted manuscripts to ERIC and share data no later than publication or five years after the award end date [663](#cite:663).

name: NHPRC weighted review criteria
what: NHPRC announcements publish the percentage weight of each review criterion, and editions applicants may respond to anonymous reviewer comments before the Commission considers the proposal [698](#cite:698) [696](#cite:696).

name: NRSA stipend levels
what: [NIH](#term:nih) sets Kirschstein-NRSA [stipends](#term:stipend) once a fiscal year in a Guide notice, after its [appropriation](#term:appropriations-act). For awards made with FY 2026 funds: undergraduates $14,916; predoctoral $29,364; postdoctoral $63,480 at 0 years of experience, $63,900 at 1, $64,380 at 2, $66,948 at 3, $69,180 at 4, $71,748 at 5, $74,424 at 6 and $77,076 at 7 or more [732](#cite:732). The levels apply only to awards made with that year's funds, and earlier awards are not adjusted [732](#cite:732). FY 2025 levels were $28,788 predoctoral and $62,232 to $75,564 postdoctoral [733](#cite:733). No FY 2027 notice was listed on 2026-10-04 [731](#cite:731).

name: NRSA tuition and fees
what: [NIH](#term:nih) pays 60% of actual tuition up to a yearly ceiling: $16,000 for predoctoral trainees and fellows ($21,000 in dual-degree programmes) and $4,500 for postdoctoral ($16,000 for formal degree-granting training); the FY 2026 notice left these unchanged [732](#cite:732).

name: NRSA institutional allowance and training-related expenses
what: An [individual fellowship](#term:f-award) carries an [institutional allowance](#term:institutional-allowance), and a [training grant](#term:t32) carries training-related expenses, to cover health insurance, supplies, equipment, books and travel. For FY 2026 both are $4,750 predoctoral and $12,400 postdoctoral, or $3,650 and $11,300 for fellows at federal and for-profit institutions [732](#cite:732) [736](#cite:736). A fellowship pays no [indirect costs](#term:indirect-costs); the allowance covers the cost of administering it [736](#cite:736).

name: NRSA childcare costs
what: An [NRSA](#term:nrsa) fellow may request $3,000 per budget period toward care by a licensed provider for children under 13, or disabled and under 18 [810]. On institutional training grants NIH has, since April 25, 2025, provided the $3,000 for 25% of the full-time trainee slots, and institutions with more eligible trainees ask for an [administrative supplement](#term:supplement) [788](#cite:788).

name: NRSA service payback obligation
what: A person incurs a service [payback obligation](#term:service-obligation) for the first 12 months of postdoctoral [NRSA](#term:nrsa) support [737](#cite:737). It is discharged by an equal number of months of further postdoctoral NRSA support, or of health-related research, research training or teaching averaging at least 20 hours a week; service must start within 2 years of the end of support [769](#cite:769). [NIH](#term:nih) may extend the time, waive the obligation where compliance is impossible or a substantial hardship, or require repayment with interest within 3 years [769](#cite:769).

name: Limits on years of NRSA support
what: An individual may receive up to 5 years of aggregate [NRSA](#term:nrsa) support at the predoctoral level (6 for dual-degree training) and up to 3 years at the postdoctoral level, counting [training grant](#term:t32) appointments and individual fellowships together [736](#cite:736) [737](#cite:737).

name: NRSA full-time training and concurrent awards
what: [NRSA](#term:nrsa) fellows and trainees train full time, normally 40 hours a week, and may not hold the award together with another federally sponsored fellowship or similar federal award that provides a [stipend](#term:stipend) [737](#cite:737) [750](#cite:750).

name: Fellowship review criteria (three criteria since January 25, 2025)
what: Fellowship applications are scored on three criteria: Candidate's Goals, Preparedness and Potential; Research Training Plan; and Commitment to Candidate, Mentoring and Training Environment [736](#cite:736). The three replaced five scored criteria for due dates on or after January 25, 2025; grades are no longer required or allowed, and the sponsor's section was restructured [794](#cite:794).

name: Reference letters for fellowships and career awards
what: Referees submit letters directly through [eRA Commons](#term:era-commons), not through [Grants.gov](#term:grants-gov), and a fellowship application without the required letters is not reviewed [784](#cite:784) [736](#cite:736). The parent [K01](#term:k-award) notice routes letters the same way [744](#cite:744). The number of letters is given in [NIH](#term:nih)'s application guide, which this sweep did not read [784](#cite:784).

name: Fellowship training abroad
what: A fellowship candidate may ask to train abroad but must justify in detail why the foreign setting is more appropriate than a domestic one; [NIH](#term:nih) funds foreign training only when the scientific advantages are clear [736](#cite:736) [737](#cite:737). The May 2026 reminder on foreign components does not mention fellows or trainees [785](#cite:785). The 2026 notices for F99/K00 and K12 state that NIH no longer issues awards that involve foreign [subawards](#term:subaward) [741](#cite:741) [753](#cite:753).

name: K award effort requirement
what: A mentored K awardee commits a minimum of 75% of full-time professional effort, 9 person-months, to the career development programme; the rest may go to other duties that do not interfere [744](#cite:744). The [K99/R00](#term:k-award) allows 50% for certain surgical specialties, and the mid-career K24 is set at 25 to 50% [743](#cite:743) [747](#cite:747).

name: K award salary and research development support (set by each institute)
what: The parent K notices do not state one NIH-wide salary figure: each participating institute provides salary, fringe benefits and research development support at its own level, published in a Table of IC-Specific Information [744](#cite:744). [NIH](#term:nih)'s page of institute considerations, as returned, shows salary figures from $75,000 to $125,000 [805](#cite:805). Total salary from federal sources may not exceed the legislated maximum, the [Executive Level II](#term:salary-cap) rate of $228,000 from January 1, 2026 [744](#cite:744) [21](#cite:21). Salary for mentors is not allowed [744](#cite:744).

name: Prior awards that end eligibility for a mentored K award
what: Current and former [principal investigators](#term:principal-investigator) of an [NIH](#term:nih) [R01](#term:r01), P01 or P50, and holders of another major individual [career award](#term:nsf-career), are not eligible for a mentored [K award](#term:k-award); holders of [R03](#term:r21-r03), R21/R33, R34/U34, R36 and SBIR/STTR awards, and scholars on institutional K12 or KL2 programmes, remain eligible [744](#cite:744). From May 28, 2025 to July 31, 2026 NIH excepted people whose mentored K award ended early on or after January 1, 2025 [786](#cite:786).

name: One career development application under review at a time
what: An individual may not have two or more competing [NIH](#term:nih) career development applications pending review at the same time, though a research project [grant](#term:grant) application without substantial overlap may be submitted alongside [744](#cite:744) [743](#cite:743).

name: Six-application limit as it applies to fellowships and career awards
what: [NIH](#term:nih) accepts six new, [renewal](#term:renewal), [resubmission](#term:resubmission) or revision applications per [principal investigator](#term:principal-investigator) per calendar year; the policy applies to all [activity codes](#term:activity-code) except T codes and R13, and names no exception for F or K codes [12](#cite:12). A [training grant](#term:t32) (T) application therefore does not count against its programme director's six [12](#cite:12).

name: Indirect costs on training and career awards (8 percent)
what: [K awards](#term:k-award), K12 programmes, [T32](#term:t32) and T35 training grants and R25 research education [grants](#term:grant) are reimbursed for [indirect costs](#term:indirect-costs) at 8% of [modified total direct costs](#term:mtdc), not at the organization's [negotiated rate](#term:nicra) [744](#cite:744) [753](#cite:753) [750](#cite:750) [756](#cite:756). On training grants the base excludes tuition and fees, consortium costs in excess of $25,000 and equipment [750]. Individual fellowships pay none [736]. The R00 phase of the K99/R00 uses the institution's own rate, inside the $249,000 yearly total [743](#cite:743).

name: Reorganization of K awards into KR1, KC1, KS1 and KT1/R00
what: For due dates on or after October 12, 2027 [NIH](#term:nih) replaces most individual K codes with four: KR1 (from [K01](#term:k-award), K21, K25, K32), KC1 (from K08, K23, K38), KS1 (from K02, K07, K18, K24, K26) and KT1/R00 (from K99, K22); K00, K12, K43 and K76 are unchanged [742](#cite:742). From then K applications need no [Data Management and Sharing Plan](#term:data-management-plan) and K funds may not pay for the conduct of a clinical trial [742](#cite:742) [758](#cite:758). Active notices under the current codes expire by July 13, 2027 [742](#cite:742).

name: Two-phase transition awards (F99/K00 and K99/R00)
what: Both awards have a mentored first phase and a second phase that starts only after a step [NIH](#term:nih) must approve. For the [K99/R00](#term:k-award) the awardee must have accepted a tenure-track, full-time assistant professor position or equivalent by the end of the K99 period [743](#cite:743). For the F99/K00 the fellow must finish the PhD and take a postdoctoral position at a different institution with a different mentor, and the new institution files K00 materials at least 4 months ahead [741](#cite:741).

name: Statement on trainee and scholar selection in training notices
what: The parent [T32](#term:t32) notice, the 2026 parent K12 notice and the NIGMS BURT notice each state that funded programmes may not use the race, ethnicity or sex of a trainee, scholar or faculty candidate as an eligibility or selection criterion, and that [NIH](#term:nih) does not use them in review or funding decisions [750](#cite:750) [753](#cite:753) [797](#cite:797). The 2026 parent R25 notice carries the second half of that statement [756](#cite:756).

name: NIH funding notices posted only on Grants.gov from FY 2026
what: From fiscal year 2026 [NIH](#term:nih) no longer posts [notices of funding opportunity](#term:nofo) in the NIH Guide; [Grants.gov](#term:grants-gov) is the single official source, and the Guide carries policy and informational notices [9](#cite:9). The 2026 [parent notices](#term:parent-announcement) for F99/K00, K12 and R25 were found on Grants.gov, and the NIH Guide address tried for PA-27-037 returned 'not found' on 2026-10-04 [740](#cite:740) [752](#cite:752) [755](#cite:755).

name: Early-stage investigator status and training awards
what: The standing record nih-early-stage-investigator gives the rule. For this family the point is that [NIH](#term:nih) keeps a list of [grants](#term:grant) a person can hold and still count as an early-stage investigator, since the status ends only with a substantial independent NIH research award [138](#cite:138). In May 2025 NIH extended the status automatically for people whose window ran out during the first half of 2025, with October 2025 as the last submission [787](#cite:787).

name: Published success rates for fellowships, career awards and training grants
what: [NIH](#term:nih) publishes competing applications, awards, [success rates](#term:success-rate) and funding for fellowships, [career development awards](#term:k-award) and [training grants](#term:t32) by [activity code](#term:activity-code) and institute, as downloadable report files [26](#cite:26). The files could not be read in this sweep, so no rate is recorded [26](#cite:26).

name: Loan repayment application cycle
what: The Extramural [Loan Repayment Program](#term:loan-repayment) takes applications once a year from September 1; the current cycle closes November 19, 2026 [763](#cite:763). In the previous cycle the closing date was moved from November 20 to December 4, 2025, with [peer review](#term:merit-review) in February to April and awards in June to August [766](#cite:766).

name: Who receives an NSF fellowship award
what: [NSF](#term:nsf) fellowships differ in who applies and who is paid [837](#cite:837) [818](#cite:818) [825](#cite:825). In the biology, mathematical sciences, astronomy, and atmospheric and geospace postdoctoral fellowships the person applies and the award is made to the individual [837](#cite:837) [840](#cite:840) [842](#cite:842) [880](#cite:880). In [GRFP](#term:grfp) the person applies but the funds are awarded to the institution where the fellow enrols [818](#cite:818). In EGFP, NRT, S-STEM and Noyce the institution applies and chooses the people [825](#cite:825) [828](#cite:828) [856](#cite:856) [858](#cite:858). The last Earth sciences fellowship [solicitation](#term:program-solicitation) moved from paying individuals to paying the host institution [850](#cite:850).

name: GRFP fellowship period and tenure
what: A Graduate Research Fellowship gives three years of financial support inside a five-year fellowship period [818](#cite:818). Funds are paid for fellows who are "on tenure"; the institution administers the award, and the fellowship can move to another institution after the first fellowship year [818](#cite:818).

name: Cost-of-education allowance
what: Beside the [stipend](#term:stipend), [NSF](#term:nsf) pays the fellow's institution a [cost-of-education allowance](#term:institutional-allowance): $16,000 per tenure year in GRFP and EGFP, and not less than $16,000 per stipend-funded trainee in NRT [818](#cite:818) [825](#cite:825) [828](#cite:828). In [GRFP](#term:grfp) the institution must exempt the fellow from tuition and required fees and bears any tuition and fees above the allowance [818](#cite:818).

name: GRFP Honorable Mention
what: [NSF](#term:nsf) gives Honorable Mention to meritorious [GRFP](#term:grfp) applicants who do not receive a fellowship offer [818](#cite:818). In the FY 2026 competition 1,470 applicants were named [861](#cite:861). An Honorable Mention within the last three years is what makes a person eligible to be an EGFP fellow [825](#cite:825).

name: GRFP applications returned without review
what: [NSF](#term:nsf) may return a [GRFP](#term:grfp) application without review for formatting failures, missing documents, or because the applicant does not meet the rules on academic status, degree programme, field of study or proposed research [861](#cite:861). The FY 2027 [solicitation](#term:program-solicitation) tells applicants to read the lists of ineligible degree programmes, areas of study and proposed research [818](#cite:818).

name: CAREER one-per-year and three-competition limit
what: An investigator may submit one CAREER proposal per annual competition and may not take part in more than three CAREER competitions [815](#cite:815).

name: CAREER departmental letter
what: A CAREER proposal must contain one, and only one, letter from the investigator's department head or equivalent official; it confirms eligibility and states the department's support for the integrated research and education plan and for mentoring [815](#cite:815).

name: CAREER minimum award size
what: CAREER sets a floor, not a ceiling: at least $400,000 over five years including indirect costs, and at least $500,000 in BIO, ENG and the Office of Polar Programs [815](#cite:815) [816](#cite:816).

name: PECASE nomination from CAREER awardees
what: Each year [NSF](#term:nsf) picks its nominees for the Presidential Early [Career Awards](#term:nsf-career) for Scientists and Engineers from the most meritorious recent CAREER awardees; a nominee must be a U.S. citizen, national or permanent resident by the time of [nomination](#term:institutional-nomination) [814](#cite:814) [815](#cite:815).

name: No indirect costs on REU participant support
what: In REU Site proposals and Supplement requests, [indirect costs](#term:indirect-costs) may not be recovered on [participant support costs](#term:participant-support-costs), the budget category that holds student [stipends](#term:stipend), housing and travel [830](#cite:830).

name: Supplements that add a person to an NSF award
what: Several [NSF](#term:nsf) routes pay for a person through an existing award, not through a new proposal: REU [Supplements](#term:supplement) for undergraduates, RET Supplements for teachers on ENG and CISE awards, and INTERN for a graduate student's non-academic internship [830](#cite:830) [854](#cite:854) [870](#cite:870). The awardee asks for the supplement; the student or teacher does not apply to NSF [830](#cite:830) [870](#cite:870). The Career-Life Balance supplement letter is archived, though the [PAPPG](#term:pappg) still lists that request type in section II.F.13, beside Facilitation Awards for Scientists and Engineers with Disabilities in II.F.7 [846](#cite:846) [257](#cite:257). The most recent letter for research assistantships for high-school students on BIO awards is also archived [889](#cite:889).

name: Institutional limits on NSF training and fellowship proposals
what: Some institutional people awards cap what one organisation may send: one EGFP proposal per competition, two NRT proposals per competition, and two S-STEM proposals per deadline [825](#cite:825) [828](#cite:828) [856](#cite:856). CAREER, REU, RET and Noyce state no limit per organisation [815](#cite:815) [830](#cite:830) [854](#cite:854) [858](#cite:858).

name: How NSF opportunity pages show that a programme is not open
what: [NSF](#term:nsf) opportunity pages use two labels for programmes with no [open call](#term:open-call) [838](#cite:838) [827](#cite:827). "This document has been archived" or "Archived funding opportunity" marks a [solicitation](#term:program-solicitation) that is no longer in force [838](#cite:838) [843](#cite:843). "Waiting for new publication" with "no upcoming due dates" marks a programme whose last solicitation has run out of deadlines and has not been replaced [827](#cite:827) [857](#cite:857) [826](#cite:826). NSF's priorities page says it continues to accept proposals to all open funding opportunities [154](#cite:154).

name: Two-step application through a state Sea Grant programme
what: For the Knauss fellowship the student applies to a state Sea [Grant](#term:grant) programme by a state deadline; the programme then sends NOAA a [letter of intent](#term:letter-of-intent) and applies through [Grants.gov](#term:grants-gov) on behalf of the students it puts forward [965](#cite:965). The NMFS-Sea Grant fellowship is also applied for through the state programme [966](#cite:966).

name: Institutional allowance in place of indirect costs
what: [NIFA](#term:nifa)'s AFRI predoctoral and postdoctoral fellowships pay the institution a $3,000 per year allowance and do not permit [indirect costs](#term:indirect-costs) [960](#cite:960). The National Needs Fellowship [grants](#term:grant) pay an [institutional allowance](#term:institutional-allowance) per fellow and do not authorise indirect costs [962](#cite:962). The Knauss fellowship allows no indirect costs [965](#cite:965).

name: Laboratory practicum or residency
what: The three DOE fellowships administered by the Krell Institute each require time at a DOE laboratory: at least 12 weeks for the CSGF, a 12-week on-site practicum for the SSGF, and two 12-week residencies for the LRGF [903](#cite:903) [905](#cite:905) [907](#cite:907).

name: Scholarship-for-service obligation
what: The SMART scholarship leads to civilian employment at a department facility after the degree [917](#cite:917). A 2019 [Federal Register](#term:federal-register) document sets the period of obligated service at the total period of degree study covered by the assistance, and lets the DoD component head set the amount to be recouped on default [919](#cite:919).

name: Student-authored proposal submitted by the university with a faculty principal investigator
what: In NASA's FINESST the university submits, a faculty mentor is the [principal investigator](#term:principal-investigator) and the student must be the primary author [949](#cite:949). In NSTGRO the [grant](#term:grant) goes to the university on behalf of the student and the faculty advisor is the principal investigator [955](#cite:955).

name: Fellow named as sole project director on an institutional application
what: In [NIFA](#term:nifa)'s AFRI predoctoral and postdoctoral fellowships the institution submits the application and the fellow is the only [project director](#term:principal-investigator) on the Key Personnel form [960](#cite:960).

name: NEH monthly rate for awards to individuals
what: [NEH](#term:neh) pays individual awards at $5,000 per month of full-time work, prorated for part-time work, to a maximum of $60,000, in the 2026 notice; the period must start on the first day of a month and end on the last day of a month [987](#cite:987) [986](#cite:986).

name: NEH Summer Stipends institutional nomination
what: The Summer [Stipends](#term:stipend) page states that institutions may nominate only one faculty member at a deadline [989](#cite:989). The exemptions from [nomination](#term:institutional-nomination) were not returned by the extraction, and the programme's status is unconfirmed [989](#cite:989) [1002](#cite:1002).

name: Eight percent indirect cost limit on a training grant
what: [HRSA](#term:hrsa)'s FY 2026 primary care [National Research Service Award](#term:nrsa) limits [indirect costs](#term:indirect-costs) to 8% of [modified total direct costs](#term:mtdc), whatever the institution's [negotiated rate](#term:nicra) [1028](#cite:1028).

name: GAANN institutional matching contribution
what: A GAANN grantee must add, from non-Federal funds, at least 25 percent of the [grant](#term:grant) amount [1017](#cite:1017) [1016](#cite:1016).

name: Fulbright U.S. Student selection chain
what: Technical review by IIE, review by the National Screening Committee, then review by U.S. embassies or binational Fulbright Commissions, the Department of State and the Fulbright Foreign Scholarship Board [1024](#cite:1024).

name: Institution applies on behalf of a named person
what: In several fellowships the person never applies to the agency: the university applies for its doctoral student (NIJ Graduate Research Fellowship; Fulbright-Hays dissertation fellowships) or for its early-career researcher ([IES](#term:ies) Early Career) and receives the money [991](#cite:991) [1012](#cite:1012) [995](#cite:995).

name: How HRSA's health workforce awards are arranged
what: The Bureau of Health Workforce describes over 60 [grant](#term:grant) programmes, made to organizations such as schools and universities, hospitals and health departments, which train students, residents and faculty [1030](#cite:1030). Beside these it runs awards to individuals in return for service, such as the Faculty [Loan Repayment Program](#term:loan-repayment) and the National Health Service Corps Loan Repayment Program, and loan funds that schools administer, such as the Nurse Faculty Loan Program [1029](#cite:1029). A person in training is normally reached through the school that holds the grant, not by applying to [HRSA](#term:hrsa) [1030](#cite:1030) [1029](#cite:1029).

name: NIOSH 70 percent trainee-cost rule
what: In [NIOSH](#term:cdc) training awards at least 70% of [direct costs](#term:direct-costs) must go to trainee costs - [stipends](#term:stipend), tuition and fees, and trainee travel - and [indirect costs](#term:indirect-costs) are limited to 8% of [modified total direct costs](#term:mtdc) [1061](#cite:1061) [1063](#cite:1063).

name: One NIOSH training application per institution
what: An institution may hold or apply for an Education and Research Center or Training Project [Grants](#term:grant), not both; for a Center only one application per institution is allowed, and a current T03 recipient is not eligible for a Center award or sub-award [1060](#cite:1060). For Training Project Grants an institution may send two academic applications or one non-academic application [1063](#cite:1063).

name: How SAMHSA posts, reviews and decides discretionary grants
what: [SAMHSA](#term:samhsa) lists its notices on its [Grants](#term:grant) Dashboard, with a separate page of [forecasts](#term:forecast) for the next fiscal year, and posts them on [Grants.gov](#term:grants-gov). Applications go through [eRA Commons ASSIST](#term:nih-assist) or [Grants.gov Workspace](#term:grants-gov-workspace). An application that is late, over the page limit or missing a required attachment is screened out and not reviewed. Peer reviewers with relevant expertise score the project narrative against point-weighted sections in the notice. The programme office and approving official make the final determination, and awards over $250,000 need National Advisory Council approval. SAM.gov responsibility records are reviewed for awards likely to exceed $250,000. After award, SAMHSA releases each later year's funds on approval of [progress reports](#term:rppr) [549](#cite:549) [1107](#cite:1107) [1113](#cite:1113) [1112](#cite:1112) [548](#cite:548).

name: SAMHSA notice structure (six steps) and the application guide
what: FY 2026 [SAMHSA](#term:samhsa) notices are laid out in six steps (Review the Opportunity; Get Ready to Apply; Build Your Application; Learn About Review and Award; Submit Your Application; Learn What Happens After Award). Each notice refers to the FY 2026 Application Guide, dated June 2026, for registration, format, budget, funding restrictions and standard terms. The project narratives in the notices read were limited to 10 or 15 pages [1112](#cite:1112) [548](#cite:548) [1205](#cite:1205).

name: SAMHSA FY 2026 funding restrictions
what: The FY 2026 application guide lists what award funds may not pay for. The list includes syringes, pipes, drug test strips for people using drugs and other drug paraphernalia; overdose hotlines whose primary function is facilitating drug use; marijuana; promotional items; building purchase or construction; inpatient treatment; direct payments to individuals to enter treatment; housing other than sober or recovery housing; housing first policies as the guide describes them; firearms; and salaries above [Executive Level II](#term:salary-cap). [Discretionary awards](#term:discretionary-grant) may not fund racial preferences, denial of the sex binary, illegal immigration, or other initiatives that compromise public safety. Minor alteration and renovation is allowed up to 25 percent of a [budget period](#term:budget-period) or $150,000, whichever is less [548](#cite:548) [1135](#cite:1135).

name: SAMHSA performance reporting in SPARS

name: Pass-through funding and subawards
what: A pass-through entity is a recipient or [subrecipient](#term:subrecipient) that gives a subaward to another organisation to carry out part of a federal programme [1799](#cite:1799). The organisation that receives the subaward is a subrecipient, and the award terms flow down to it [1799](#cite:1799) [1805](#cite:1805). A university that leads a multi-site project and a state that distributes a formula grant are both pass-through entities, and each has the same list of duties toward its subrecipients [1823](#cite:1823).
rule: Under [2 CFR 200](#term:uniform-guidance).331 the pass-through entity decides case by case whether the other party is a subrecipient or a contractor; a subrecipient determines eligibility, has its performance measured against programme objectives, makes programmatic decisions and is responsible for programme requirements, while a contractor sells goods or services in its normal business and is not subject to programme compliance requirements [1822](#cite:1822). The substance of the relationship matters more than the form of the agreement [1822](#cite:1822). Under 200.332 the pass-through entity must verify in SAM.gov that the subrecipient is not excluded; identify the subaward as a subaward and give 14 data items, including the federal award number, the [Assistance Listing](#term:assistance-listing) and the [indirect cost](#term:indirect-costs) rate; evaluate the subrecipient's fraud risk and risk of noncompliance; monitor its activities and review its reports; issue management decisions on audit findings; verify that it is audited when subpart F requires; and consider enforcement under 200.339 [1823](#cite:1823). On indirect costs the pass-through entity must accept the subrecipient's federally [negotiated rate](#term:nicra); where there is none the rate is one negotiated between the two parties or the [de minimis rate](#term:de-minimis-rate), and the pass-through entity may not require the de minimis rate of a subrecipient that has a federally negotiated rate [1823](#cite:1823) [1802](#cite:1802). Under 200.333 a recipient may, with the federal agency's [prior written approval](#term:prior-approval), make fixed amount subawards of up to $500,000 [1824]. A subrecipient submits its final reports and liquidates its obligations within 90 calendar days of the end of the subaward [1830]. Only the first $50,000 of each subaward counts in the pass-through entity's modified total [direct cost](#term:direct-costs) base [1799](#cite:1799). The [eCFR](#term:cfr) text of 200.332 current to 10/01/2026 lists the same 14 data items and the same rule that a pass-through entity must not require the de minimis rate of a subrecipient that has a rate negotiated with the Federal Government [2105](#cite:2105). The eCFR page for 200.344 returned server errors twice on 2026-10-04; the eCFR's version record for part 200 lists no issue of 200.333 or 200.344 after the amendment dated October 1, 2024 [2103](#cite:2103). The eCFR page for 200.333 did load later the same day and shows the same $500,000 ceiling with prior written approval [2116](#cite:2116).

name: Termination for convenience under Executive Order 14332
what: [Executive Order 14332](#term:executive-order-14332) directs that discretionary grants permit termination for convenience, meaning termination at the Government's choice, including when an award no longer advances agency priorities or the national interest [246](#cite:246). The order works through two channels: a revision of the [Uniform Guidance](#term:uniform-guidance) by OMB, and new terms that agencies add to their awards [246](#cite:246). On 2026-10-04 the first channel is a proposal that cannot be finalised before December 11, 2026, and the second depends on each agency's terms [1480](#cite:1480) [65](#cite:65).
rule: Section 5 of the order directs the OMB Director to revise the Uniform Guidance to clarify that discretionary grants permit termination for convenience [246](#cite:246). Section 6 directs agencies to revise the terms of existing discretionary grants to permit immediate termination for convenience, and to require written explanation for each drawdown of funds [246](#cite:246). The rule in force, 2 CFR 200.340, has no ground called termination for convenience; its fourth ground allows termination under the award terms, including, to the extent authorised by law, where an award no longer effectuates programme goals or agency priorities, and requires every termination provision to be stated clearly and unambiguously in the award [1801](#cite:1801). The District of Massachusetts declared on July 17, 2026 that this ground does not reach priorities adopted after the award was made [1869](#cite:1869). OMB's [proposed rule](#term:proposed-rule) would revise 200.340 to clarify termination of discretionary awards for discretionary reasons consistent with law [1803](#cite:1803).

name: OMB's proposed "Regulation for Federal Financial Assistance" (91 FR 32198, May 29, 2026)
what: On May 29, 2026 OMB, with the grant-making agencies as co-proposers, published a [proposed rule](#term:proposed-rule) to revise 2 [CFR](#term:cfr), including the [Uniform Guidance](#term:uniform-guidance) in part 200 [1458](#cite:1458). It would turn the guidance into a regulation that takes effect government-wide on one date, and would change rules on notices, payments, [subawards](#term:subaward), [termination](#term:termination), national policy requirements and cost items [1803](#cite:1803) [1458](#cite:1458). On 2026-10-04 it is a proposal: no final rule has been published, and section 157 of Public Law 119-103 provides that a rule arising from it shall not be issued, finalised or take effect through December 11, 2026 [1858](#cite:1858) [1480](#cite:1480). The Uniform Guidance as revised in 2024 remains the rule in force [1857](#cite:1857) [1801](#cite:1801).
rule: Comment period: Comments were due on or before July 13, 2026 in docket OMB-2026-0034; the [Federal Register](#term:federal-register) record shows 496,606 comments [1458](#cite:1458) [1858](#cite:1858). Status: OMB's regulatory agenda of August 14, 2026 lists the rule (RIN 0348-AB88) in the proposed rule stage with no date for final action [1859](#cite:1859). Section 157 of the [continuing resolution](#term:continuing-resolution) signed September 2, 2026 bars a rule "arising out of" the proposal "or a substantially similar rule" from being issued or finalised through December 11, 2026, and says a rule finalised before enactment has no force through that date; the Senate committee summary says the section retains existing guidance through December 11, 2026 [1480](#cite:1480) [1857](#cite:1857). [NIH](#term:nih) states that the resolution prohibits it from implementing the revisions through December 11, 2026 [83](#cite:83). The chair of the Senate [Appropriations](#term:appropriations-act) Committee stated on September 21, 2026 that the resolution blocks OMB's proposed rule or any substantially similar one [1891](#cite:1891). Stated objectives: improved transparency, accountability and oversight; clarification of regulatory structure; reduced recipient burden [1803](#cite:1803). Section by section, in outline, from the Federal Register text as far as it was read (through 200.111) and from its table of contents for the rest: Part 1: "guidance" becomes "regulation", relying on 31 U.S.C. 503 and 6307, with a new 1.221 for agencies that implement by policy [1803](#cite:1803). 200.1: definitions of fixed amount award and protected PII removed; Federal award date, improper payment, PII and unobligated balance changed [1803](#cite:1803). 200.101 and 200.102: a new paragraph on conflicts with agency regulations, under which subpart F and 200.340 govern [1803](#cite:1803). 200.110: OMB amendments would apply government-wide on the effective date of a final rule without separate agency rulemakings [1803](#cite:1803). 200.201 and 200.333: fixed amount awards and subawards eliminated [1803](#cite:1803). 200.202: programme design aligned with law and executive branch policy; multi-year awards encouraged [1803](#cite:1803). 200.204 to 200.206: all funding opportunities posted on [Grants.gov](#term:grants-gov), with changes to [merit review](#term:merit-review) and [risk review](#term:risk-review) [1803](#cite:1803). 200.208 and 200.211: specific conditions and award contents revised [1803](#cite:1803). New 200.218, 200.219 and 200.220: prohibitions concerning disparate-impact liability theories, discriminatory event services and covered foreign collaborations; 200.300 revised [1458](#cite:1458). 200.305: justification required for payment requests [1803](#cite:1803). 200.329 to 200.332: subaward reporting on [SAM.gov](#term:sam-gov) [1803](#cite:1803). 200.339 to 200.343: termination and suspension, to clarify termination of [discretionary awards](#term:discretionary-grant) for discretionary reasons consistent with law [1803](#cite:1803). Subpart E: changes to 200.421, 200.429, 200.432, 200.438, 200.442, 200.444, 200.450, 200.454, 200.455, 200.461, 200.467 and a new 200.477 [1458](#cite:1458). Subpart F: 200.503, 200.513, 200.514 [1458](#cite:1458). Appendices I, II, VIII and IX revised; agency chapters in Subtitle B of 2 CFR revised or added [1458](#cite:1458). From an association summary, not checked against the Federal Register text: five termination grounds including agency discretion; no hearing required for terminations other than for noncompliance; senior political appointee review of each notice under a new 200.205; advertising, conference, membership and publication costs restricted; no change to negotiated [indirect cost](#term:indirect-costs) rates; an intended effective date of October 1, 2026 for new awards only [1878](#cite:1878). Checked on 2026-10-04 against the Federal Register text, from its HTML version as far as page 32212 and from short passages of the later preamble and regulatory text returned by the Federal Register's full-text search [2092](#cite:2092) [2093](#cite:2093) [2104](#cite:2104). Termination: proposed 200.340(a) lists five grounds, (1) noncompliance by the recipient or [subrecipient](#term:subrecipient), including a failure to report subawards, (2) a determination by the agency or [pass-through entity](#term:pass-through-entity), to the extent permitted by law, that termination is in its interest, including where the award no longer effectuates programme goals, agency priorities or the national interest as they exist at the time of termination, (3) mutual agreement, (4) notification by the recipient or subrecipient, and (5) additional termination provisions in the award; awards must always include grounds (1) to (4) [2093](#cite:2093) [2104](#cite:2104). A new 200.340(d) would allow a written order to stop work, which the preamble likens to a provision of the FAR [2104](#cite:2104). On 200.342 the preamble says hearing rights continue for a remedy for noncompliance and would not be required for other types of termination unless other law expressly requires them [2093](#cite:2093). Review: proposed 200.205 keeps peer review advisory and adds a pre-issuance review, by senior appointees, of proposals selected for funding; the review must be described in the [notice of funding opportunity](#term:nofo) and may form the basis of a decision not to select an applicant [2092](#cite:2092) [2093](#cite:2093). New sections: 200.218 bars the use of awards in support of disparate-impact studies, litigation or related activities unless expressly required by law; 200.219 is headed "Prohibition of Discriminatory Event Services" and concerns public entities that are recipients or subrecipients; 200.220 prohibits obligating federal funds for covered foreign collaborations and does not prohibit collaborations paid for with non-federal funds [2104](#cite:2104) [2093](#cite:2093). Cost items: advertising and public relations costs [unallowable](#term:allowable-cost) with limited exceptions (200.421); conference attendance allowable only if expressly approved by the agency and included in the award terms (200.432); three new paragraphs in 200.450, one prohibiting the funding of voter registration activities; a new [prior approval](#term:prior-approval) requirement in 200.454; publication costs unallowable unless expressly required by statute (200.461) [2093](#cite:2093). Indirect costs: part IX of the preamble states that OMB is not proposing updates to the indirect cost rate negotiation system through the document and asks commenters not to comment on that system [2093](#cite:2093). Effective date: part XI states that OMB proposes a final rule effective by October 1, 2026, so that a single set of government-wide requirements applies to Federal awards made during fiscal year 2027, and gives a 45-day comment period [2093](#cite:2093) [2104](#cite:2104). The Federal Register record on 2026-10-04 shows no correction and no effective date for the document [1858](#cite:1858). Section 157 was re-read in the public law text on govinfo: subsection (a) bars issuing or finalising a rule to revise the Uniform Guidance through December 11, 2026, and subsection (b) denies force or effect through that date to one issued before enactment [1480](#cite:1480).
